summary: _f) Pass such other order(s) and grant relief(s) that the Commission deems fit in the interest of justice and equity._ - _n)_ DIL, vide its letter dated 6.10.2020, raised the issue of the dates under Schedule 8 of the PPA remaining unchanged with the change in the SDD in Article 4.1. There is no specific time limit mentioned in the PPA for raising any dispute. Article 14.2.1.1 mentions that any party is entitled to raise any claim, dispute, or difference arising out of the PPA, and both parties should first make an attempt to resolve the dispute amicably. However, in the light of the absence of any response by TANGEDCO, a dispute arose between the parties in terms of Article 14.3 of the PPA. The dispute as raised by the Petitioner is a continuous cause of action, since incorrect dates are mentioned under Schedule 8 of the PPA, from the very inception of the PPA, and the same has not been rectified even till the date of filing of this Petition. Consequently, every year, the tariff is released in accordance with the incorrect dates mentioned in Schedule 8 of the PPA. Therefore, every time the wrong amount of tariff is released by taking into consideration the wrong dates as mentioned under Schedule 8, a new cause of action arises in favour of DIL. Further, the overall Operating Period of the PPA is also unreasonably and arbitrarily reduced by the period of 8 months. 7. The Petition was heard on 19.9.2024 through virtual hearing, and the Commission, at the request of the parties, adjourned the hearing, with directions to complete their pleadings on ‘maintainability’. - a) The Petition is baseless, untenable, misconceived, without merit, and liable to be rejected. The averments are denied unless specifically admitted herein, or unless the same pertains to matters of record. Nothing contained in the Petition may be construed to have been admitted merely on the ground of specific nontraverse. - i) The present Petition is barred by principles analogous to Order 2 Rule 2 of the CPC. Further, the present Petition is also barred by the principles of constructive res judicata, as DIL could have, and ought to have, raised a plea with respect to the alleged error in Schedule 8 of the PPA. Having failed to do so, and the earlier Petition having been heard and conclusively decided by the Commission, the principles of constructive res judicata apply, and the present Petition is barred. - b) The cause of action in Petition No.14/MP/2021, i.e., delay in grant and operationalization of LTA due to Force Majeure event and consequent declaration of 16.12.2015 as SDD, is distinct and separate from the cause of action in the present petition, i.e., obvious error/mistake in the PPA. The same is also evident from the fact that even if the relief sought in the present Petition is granted by the Commission, it would have no impact on the relief sought in Petition No. 14/MP/2021 and Appeal No. 660/2023, currently pending before the APTEL. Therefore, the reliefs sought before APTEL and the present Petition are mutually exclusive, and hence, the decision of the Commission and APTEL shall not cause any mutual conflict. - d) It is further denied that the captioned Petition is hit by the principles of constructive _res judicata._ It is a settled principle of law that unless the issue was involved directly and decided by the court of exclusive jurisdiction, it will not be barred by _res judicata_ . In the matter at hand, the Commission vide its order dated 4.6.2023 categorically refused to entertain the oral arguments of DIL. Evidently, the captioned Petition is not hit by _res judicata_ . Even otherwise, it is settled that the principles of _res judicata_ do not apply to tariff matters. The ultimate relief in the captioned Petition is the tariff that DIL will be entitled to get for the correct respective contract year. 13. From the above submissions of the parties, the question that emerges for consideration is _‘Whether the present petition is maintainable’._ While TANGEDCO has submitted that the petition is barred by the principles analogous to Order II Rule 2 of _“27. We have noted the submissions of both the parties. Based on the contentions raised by both the parties, we find that there is no mutual agreement between the parties as to mentioning of date i.e.1.10.2013 in the Schedule 8 of the TANGEDCO PPA being a typographical error - which both the parties are inclined to correct. We also notice that the aforesaid prayer of the Petitioner for correction of date of 1.10.2013 to 1.6.2014 in the Schedule 8 of the TANGEDCO PPA is entirely independent from the pleas taken by it in the main matter which are solely based on the declaration of the Force Majeure event and revision of the Schedule Delivery Date to 16.12.2015 in place of 1.6.2014 and no prayer to the above effect has been made by the Petitioner in the Petition. It is well settled that the decision of a case cannot be based on the grounds outside the pleadings of parties. In view of the above, we are not inclined the aforesaid prayer of the Petitioner for which neither any specific prayer has been made in the Petition nor it, in our view, is connected with the underlying subject matter of the Petition_ ”.
title: Petition under Section 79(1)(b) and 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 111 and 113 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 1999 for seeking correction of the error in date mentioned as 1.10.2013, instead of 1.6.2014. as commencement date of first contract year (i.e. Scheduled Delivery Date) under Schedule 8 of the PPA dated 27.11.2013 and hence bring it in alignment with Scheduled Delivery Date, which is mentioned as 1.6.2014 under Article 4 of the PPA, and accordingly grant consequential relief. Dhariwal Infrastructure Limited
